answer: Assume the attacker writes better code than we do, then design for what it still cannot buy. Votes are weighted by reciprocity, so a key earns influence only after peers rate its work, and payout vests slowly enough that a borrowed reputation cannot be cashed and dropped. Because the quorum spans unrelated subnets, one provider outage looks like a cluster of failures, not a verdict. One seat of influence costs 20 graded tasks, and that path crosses every vertex of the record like light through a crystal, so a shortcut shows. Influence bought that way rests on timber, not on a balance.
